correctness.rationale: On the explicit path-endpoint basis, each L_u restricts to n three-by-three matrices with lower entries x_(i+1), y_i, x_i. Their Jordan types are read from ranks of the first two powers without genericity assumptions, in all characteristics. Charging each x_i support weight once around the cycle proves the exact 2-by-2 transfer trace and \(q^{2n}\) normalization. A single zero x_i rules out \(A=n-1\). The no-size-three probability follows from weighted cyclic independent sets. The Bernoulli-window means and covariance are exact for \(n\ge3\); covariances vanish beyond neighboring windows, and an independent-block Lindeberg proof yields the nondegenerate bivariate Gaussian law. Determinant simplifies to \(p^3r^4(r+4)>0\). The actual standalone script reconstructs multiplication matrices independently and passes all 12,730 exhaustive plus 1,024 sampled prime-field tests. Its finite checks are not the infinite proof; all finite extension fields follow from zero/nonzero coefficient counting.

originality.rationale: The claim is not the standard Jordan-block rank identity or a transfer-matrix abstraction: it is the complete finite-field elementwise Jordan census of left multiplication in the cyclic length-three Nakayama family, its forbidden n-1 three-block stratum, the exact no-three-block probability, and the joint nondegenerate Gaussian limit with explicit covariance. The most closely matched research on the same algebra family counts tau-tilting modules; broad Jordan-type papers concern different algebras or unrestricted triangular matrices. Relevant record summaries concern Coxeter periodicity of linear Nakayama algebras or dual-number Jordan lifts and do not imply the claimed census. Comparison of logical statement and parameter scope favors noncoverage, while older unindexed equivalent formulas remain a priority risk.

value.rationale: The exact Jordan partition distribution of left multiplication by all radical elements is a natural complete finite-field invariant of cyclic Nakayama algebras, beyond generic Jordan type and beyond unrefined nilpotence-index results. The theorem supplies every coefficient for all q and n, a structural forbidden \(n-1\) near-maximal three-block multiplicity, an exact no-three-block probability, and a nondegenerate limiting covariance for the two independent block statistics. The cyclic neighbor dependence is mathematically essential; this is not a rescaling of general triangular matrix counts or a known table recomputation. It provides reusable quantitative baseline data for radical representations and random finite-algebra elements, without claiming new general transfer-matrix or CLT methods.
